report:
Reviewed the complete meta.book.crates_landing claim and both ordinary implementation associations (book.rs and spec.rs), plus its sole ordinary test curated_crates_landing_preserves_prose_and_links_to_generated_chapters. No TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist.

Source assessment: render_sections applies SpecIndex::render_chapter to handwritten content; render_chapter copies text outside replacement spans. generate_crates updates the landing's sub_items, not its prose, nests module chapters inside their crate chapters, and retains parent names under Crates. The explorer is generated as a separate asset and embedded in generated chapters. chapter_replacements resolves local .sage destinations through the published chapter inventory to HTML URLs, retains entity fragments, and rejects unpublished Sage targets. The captured actual Crates README supplies curated subsystem introductions linking to modeled crate/module chapters. These mechanisms account for preservation, curated navigation, hierarchy, absence of a replacement landing explorer, and source-to-rendered links.

Test assessment: the annotated integration test invokes the actual preprocess executable with a modeled fixture, handwritten tour and entity-fragment link. Visible assertions require successful processing, preserved tour text, symbols.html#item:demo::symbols::Item, no landing iframe, rewritten companion-guide link, Design/Crates/demo parent names and the landing home URL in the generated asset. The captured fixture, recursive chapter collector and script_data helper establish the setup and inspected output. Together with the explicit construction of crate/module sub_items, these assertions adequately exercise the claimed reading-map behavior; replacing prose with an explorer or failing URL conversion would be detected.

Baseline verification: exact byte comparison confirmed current book.rs and spec.rs equal the historical implementation sources. The full test-file delta only migrates other anchor-page review fixtures/assertions to start/record and updates another test to read claim fragments; the associated test and its helpers are unchanged. I independently reassessed the current claim-specific rationale and assertions, rather than treating that equality as approval.

Execution: I ran review start, dependency review reads, byte comparisons and review record; I ran no behavioral tests or workspace build and made no source edits. The coordinator's reported 321 passing functional sage-meta tests and successful root build are separate execution evidence, not my own results.
